config.title: Build a notes app with create edit delete and search

intro.title: Build a notes app with create edit delete and search
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple notes application from scratch using plain JavaScript. You will learn to create, edit, delete, and search through notes, all within a single web page. The core programming concept involves managing application state with an array of objects and manipulating the DOM to reflect changes. You'll use fundamental JavaScript constructs like functions, event listeners, and array methods to implement the app's functionality.
intro.usecase: This notes app pattern appears in countless real-world applications where users need to manage dynamic content collections. You'll find it in project management tools like Trello (creating/editing cards), customer relationship systems (managing contact records), and content management dashboards (handling articles or products). As a developer, you'll implement similar create-edit-delete-search functionality for admin panels, data tables, and user-generated content interfaces. Mastering these core operations prepares you for building interactive features in web applications across industries.

objectives: Construct a user interface with input fields and buttons for note creation and search
Implement state management to store and update an array of note objects
Configure event handlers to add new notes and delete existing notes
Manipulate the DOM to render the current list of notes dynamically
Integrate a search input to filter the displayed notes based on user input
Initialize a form to edit note content and update the state accordingly
Apply conditional rendering to show edit forms only for selected notes

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from 'react'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have the necessary imports to start building your notes app with state management.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: import React and useState from the 'react' package.

steps.title: Create the main App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns an empty div element.
steps.hint: Define the component using either a function declaration or arrow function syntax, and make sure it returns a JSX div.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the App component here
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is defined and returns an empty div.
successCriteria: A functional component named App is created and returns a JSX div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've created a component named App that returns a div element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Check that you've defined a function named App that returns a JSX div.

steps.title: Initialize notes state with sample data
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, initialize a state variable named 'notes' using useState. Set its initial value to an array containing at least one sample note object with properties: id, title, and content.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported. The initial value should be an array of objects, like [{ id: 1, title: 'Sample note', content: 'This is a sample note' }].
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: initializing a state array
const [items, setItems] = useState([{ id: 1, name: 'Item 1' }]);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable 'notes' initialized with an array containing at least one note object.
successCriteria: The 'notes' state variable is declared with useState, and its initial value is an array with at least one object having id, title, and content properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that 'notes' is initialized as an array with at least one note object containing id, title, and content properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The notes state isn't initialized correctly. Make sure to use useState to declare 'notes' and set its initial value to an array of note objects.

steps.title: Create addNote handler
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, create a function named addNote that takes two parameters: title and content. The function should create a new note object with a unique id and add it to the notes state using setNotes.
steps.hint: You can generate a unique id using Date.now() or Math.random(). The new note object should have id, title, and text properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have an addNote function that creates new note objects and updates the notes state.
successCriteria: The addNote function is defined with parameters title and content, creates a new note object with id, title, and text properties, and updates the notes state using setNotes.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your addNote function takes both title and content parameters, creates a complete note object, and properly updates the state using setNotes.
steps.feedbackWrong: The addNote function isn't quite right. It should take title and content parameters, create a new note object with id, title, and text properties, and update the notes state using setNotes.

steps.title: Create deleteNote handler
steps.instruction: Create a deleteNote function that takes an id parameter and removes the matching note from the notes array.
steps.hint: Use the setNotes function to update the state by filtering out the note with the given id.
steps.expectedOutcome: A deleteNote function that filters the notes array to remove a note by its id.
successCriteria: The deleteNote function is defined, takes an id parameter, and uses setNotes with filter to remove the matching note.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your deleteNote function takes an id parameter and uses setNotes to update the state by filtering out the note with that id.
steps.feedbackWrong: The deleteNote function is not correctly defined. It should take an id parameter and use setNotes with filter to remove the matching note from the notes array.

steps.title: Create updateNote handler
steps.instruction: Inside your component, create a function named updateNote that takes id and text parameters and updates the matching note in the notes array.
steps.hint: The function should use setNotes to update state. You can use map to create a new array where the note with the matching id gets its text updated.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have an updateNote function that can modify existing notes by their id.
successCriteria: The updateNote function is defined, takes id and text parameters, and uses setNotes with map to update the matching note.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function takes id and text parameters and updates the notes array correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The updateNote function isn't quite right. It should take id and text parameters and update the matching note in the notes array using setNotes.

steps.title: Create search handler
steps.instruction: Create a handleSearch function that updates the searchTerm state when the search input changes. Define it inside your App component.
steps.hint: The function should take an event parameter and call setSearchTerm with the input's value.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleSearch function is defined inside the component, ready to be used with an input's onChange event.
successCriteria: The handleSearch function is defined, takes an event parameter, and calls setSearchTerm with event.target.value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function takes an event parameter and calls setSearchTerm with event.target.value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. Remember to create a function named handleSearch that updates the searchTerm state.

steps.title: Add search input and wire to handler
steps.instruction: Inside your component's return statement, add an input element for searching notes. Set its value to the searchTerm state and its onChange event to call the handleSearch function.
steps.hint: Use an <input> element with value={searchTerm} and onChange={(e) => handleSearch(e.target.value)}.
steps.expectedOutcome: The search input will appear in the UI, allowing users to type and filter notes.
successCriteria: An input element is added with value bound to searchTerm and onChange wired to handleSearch.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added an input, but make sure it's controlled (value={searchTerm}) and the onChange calls handleSearch.
steps.feedbackWrong: The search input is missing or not properly wired. Check the instruction and try again.

steps.title: Add form for creating notes and wire to addNote
steps.instruction: Add a form element with an input for the note title, a textarea for the note content, and a submit button. Wire the form's onSubmit event to call the addNote handler with the form values.
steps.hint: Create a form with two input fields and a button. Use the onSubmit event on the form to trigger your addNote function.
steps.expectedOutcome: A form with title input, content textarea, and submit button appears in the UI. The form's onSubmit event is connected to the addNote handler.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your form has both input fields and the onSubmit event is properly connected to addNote.
steps.feedbackWrong: The form isn't complete yet. Check that you have all required form elements and the onSubmit event handler.

steps.title: Display filtered notes list
steps.instruction: Inside the return statement, add a section to display the filtered notes list by mapping through notes filtered by searchTerm. For each note, display its text content.
steps.hint: Filter the notes array based on whether the note's text includes the searchTerm, then map through the filtered array to render each note.
steps.expectedOutcome: The app will display a list of notes filtered by the search term, with each note's text shown.
successCriteria: The code includes a filtered notes list rendered in the return statement, using filter and map methods.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to filter the notes based on searchTerm and map through the filtered array to render each note's text.
steps.feedbackWrong: The filtered notes list is not correctly implemented. Ensure you filter the notes array and map through it to display each note's text.

steps.title: Add edit and delete buttons to each note
steps.instruction: Inside the map function that renders each note, add an edit button and a delete button next to the note text. The delete button should call deleteNote with the note's id when clicked.
steps.hint: Add two button elements inside the list item. Use onClick handlers: one for delete that calls deleteNote(note.id), and one for edit that you'll implement later.
steps.expectedOutcome: Each note in the list will now have two buttons: 'Edit' and 'Delete'. Clicking Delete will remove the note from the list.
successCriteria: Each note list item contains an edit button
Each note list item contains a delete button
Delete button has onClick handler calling deleteNote with note.id
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some buttons, but make sure each note has both edit and delete buttons, and the delete button properly calls deleteNote with the note's id.
steps.feedbackWrong: The buttons aren't properly added. Check that you're adding both buttons inside the map function, and that the delete button has the correct onClick handler.
